annotation_description: Playing Ancient Tomb first instead of Seat of the Synod is suboptimal. With this hand (Ancient Tomb, Seat of the Synod, Chalice of the Void, 2x Mishra's Bauble, 2x Mox Opal), the ideal line is: play Seat of the Synod, cast both Mishra's Baubles (free), cast Mox Opal (free, now have 3 artifacts for Metalcraft), then tap Mox Opal for one mana + tap Seat of the Synod for one mana to cast Chalice of the Void on X=1. This deploys Chalice on 1 without taking any damage from Ancient Tomb. Ancient Tomb can be played next turn. By playing Ancient Tomb first, the player will need to tap it (taking 2 damage) to cast Chalice, or end up with a suboptimal Chalice on X=0 or miss the turn 1 Chalice on 1 entirely.

Casting the second Mishra's Bauble before Mox Opal is fine for enabling Metalcraft, but the player should consider whether casting Chalice of the Void on 1 (using Ancient Tomb for {C}{C}) is the priority play here. With Ancient Tomb already tapped (it was used earlier), the sequencing matters. However, the real issue is more subtle: by casting the second Bauble now, they're building toward Metalcraft, but they should consider whether Mox Opal into Chalice on 1 is achievable this turn. With Ancient Tomb already tapped, they need Mox Opal's mana. The sequence should be: cast Mox Opal first (it's legendary, so one will be sacrificed if both are cast), then cast Bauble to reach 3 artifacts for Metalcraft, then tap Mox Opal for mana. Actually, casting Bauble before Mox Opal is equivalent here since both cost 0 - the order doesn't matter for reaching Metalcraft. But there's a key consideration: if they cast both Mox Opals, the legend rule destroys one, leaving them at only 2 artifacts (Bauble + 1 Mox Opal + Bauble = 3). The sequencing is actually fine - cast Bauble to get to 3 artifacts before needing Metalcraft. This appears reasonable.

Karakas produces white mana which doesn't cast anything in hand. The hand has Life from the Loam (needs green) and Boseiju channel (needs green). Playing a green source would enable casting spells next turn, while Karakas's white mana is currently useless. Additionally, Wasteland could be considered to destroy Ancient Tomb on a future turn after establishing a green source.

Casting a second Mox Opal is a waste due to the Legend Rule - having two legendary permanents with the same name forces you to sacrifice one immediately. The player already has a Mox Opal on the battlefield, so playing a second one means one goes straight to the graveyard for no benefit. While it does trigger Kappa Cannoneer if it were on the battlefield (it's not yet), and it briefly puts an artifact onto the battlefield before legend-ruling one away, the net result is losing a card for essentially nothing. The player should have cast Urza's Bauble (which stays on the battlefield, contributes to artifact count, and provides card advantage) or cast Chalice of the Void on an appropriate number.

By casting Chalice of the Void before Urza's Bauble, they missed enabling metalcraft on Mox Opal (which needs 3 artifacts). Casting Urza's Bauble first (free, mana value 0) would give a third artifact, activate metalcraft, and provide 4 mana total—opening the option of Chalice on X=2 while still getting the Bauble's card draw and hand information.

chosen_display: Urza's Bauble — {T}, Sacrifice {this}: Look at a card at random i... [Activate]
annotation_description: By sacrificing Urza's Bauble before casting Kappa Cannoneer, Libby lost an artifact needed for Improvise, making it impossible to cast Kappa Cannoneer this turn. With Urza's Bauble still on the battlefield, they could play Ancient Tomb from hand and cast Kappa Cannoneer for exactly 6 mana: Ancient Tomb (CC) + Seat of the Synod (U) + Mox Opal (1) + Improvise Chalice + Improvise Urza's Bauble. A turn-2 Kappa Cannoneer is an extremely powerful play that is now delayed by at least a turn.

Playing Dark Depths on turn 2 without Thespian's Stage or any way to remove ice counters efficiently is premature. Dark Depths produces no mana and the 3-mana-per-counter activation is incredibly slow. Meanwhile, the opponent has Chalice of the Void on 1 (blanking 1-mana spells) and is developing an artifact-based board. Playing a mana-producing land like Forest or Yavimaya would be more immediately useful - Forest provides green mana for Life from the Loam or Boseiju's channel ability, and Yavimaya makes all lands Forests (including Karakas), enabling green mana production across the board. Dark Depths without a combo piece is just a dead land drop.

Gem25F Libby passed the turn without casting Pinnacle Emissary via its Warp cost of {U/R}, which only requires 1 mana. This would have provided a 3/3 attacker for the turn and artifact synergy triggers. While it exiles at end step, it can be recast later and provides free damage/pressure.

Gem25F Libby has Ancient Tomb (untapped on battlefield), Seat of the Synod, Mox Opal (on battlefield with metalcraft active from Mox Opal + Seat of the Synod + Chalice of the Void), and another Ancient Tomb in hand. They could cast Pinnacle Emissary for its Warp cost of {U/R} by tapping Mox Opal or Seat of the Synod for blue. Even at full cost {1}{U}{R}, they have Ancient Tomb ({C}{C}) + Mox Opal (U or R) + Seat of the Synod (U) = they can produce {C}{C}{U}{U} or {C}{C}{U}{R}, which covers {1}{U}{R}. Additionally, they could play the second Ancient Tomb as their land drop (though they said they already made it). Even without a second land drop, casting Pinnacle Emissary is clearly possible this turn - either at warp cost for just {U/R}, or at full cost using their available mana. This is a meaningful missed play that would put a 3/3 creature on the board that generates tokens when artifacts are cast.

Playing Forest instead of Yavimaya, Cradle of Growth is suboptimal. Yavimaya would make all lands (including Karakas and Dark Depths) tap for green mana in addition to their other types, immediately giving 3 green sources instead of just 1. This would enable casting Life from the Loam this turn and make Boseiju's channel ability easier to activate. Forest provides only a single green source and doesn't synergize with the rest of the mana base.

Cast Disruptor Flute before making a land drop. Playing Yavimaya, Cradle of Growth first would make all lands Forests, providing more green mana flexibility. Additionally, channeling Boseiju to destroy Chalice of the Void (clearing the way for 1-mana spells) or playing Wasteland to threaten Ancient Tomb may have been higher-impact plays. Disruptor Flute is a reasonable card but the sequencing is wrong - land should come first to maximize options.

Gem25F Libby had enough mana to cast Kappa Cannoneer by first playing Ancient Tomb as their land drop (2nd Ancient Tomb providing {C}{C}{C}{C} total + Seat of the Synod for {U} + Mox Opal for 1 color + Chalice of the Void tapped for improvise = 6+ mana for {5}{U}). Kappa Cannoneer would enter as a 5/5 unblockable threat. Even without the land drop, Pinnacle Emissary was castable at {1}{U}{R} using Ancient Tomb + Seat of the Synod + Mox Opal for {R}. Instead, the player incorrectly assessed that no spells were castable and passed the entire turn.

Libby has enough mana to cast Pinnacle Emissary at full cost ({1}{U}{R}) using Ancient Tomb ({C}{C}), Seat of the Synod ({U}), and Mox Opal ({R}), or even just via Warp for {U/R}. Instead they passed, claiming insufficient mana. Deploying Pinnacle Emissary would establish a threat and its trigger would create tokens when casting future artifact spells, synergizing with the deck's gameplan.

Playing Wasteland over Yavimaya, Cradle of Growth misses significant mana development. Yavimaya would make Dark Depths tap for green mana, effectively giving an extra green source. With Yavimaya, all 4 lands would produce green, enabling more flexible casting of the multiple green spells in hand (2x Life from the Loam, Malevolent Rumble, Boseiju channel). Wasteland can be played on a later turn or the opponent's lands can be handled via Boseiju's channel ability.

annotation_description: Dark Depths has 10 ice counters and removing them one at a time at 3 mana each costs 30 total mana - this is an incredibly slow and inefficient plan without Thespian's Stage or Vampire Hexmage to combo. Meanwhile, the opponent has Chalice of the Void (likely on 0 given the 0-cost artifacts in their deck) and is building toward threats like Kappa Cannoneer. The player should be using Boseiju to destroy Chalice of the Void or advancing their board with Malevolent Rumble to find combo pieces or threats. Playing Yavimaya first would also enable better mana. Spending 3 mana to remove a single ice counter when you have no way to quickly remove the other 9 is essentially wasting a turn.

Gem25F Libby had exactly enough mana to cast Pinnacle Emissary ({1}{U}{R}) using Ancient Tomb for {C}{C}, Seat of the Synod for {U}, and Mox Opal (with Metalcraft active from 3 artifacts) for {R}. The game engine confirmed it as a legal play option. Passing the turn without deploying a 3/3 creature that generates tokens from artifact spells is a significant missed opportunity.

Gem25F Libby could have cast Pinnacle Emissary for its Warp cost of {U/R} using Seat of the Synod. While it would be exiled at the next end step, it would provide a temporary 3/3 body and set up future casting from exile. The game engine listed it as a valid castable option.

Playing Boseiju as a land instead of Yavimaya wastes Boseiju's powerful channel ability (instant-speed artifact/enchantment/nonbasic land destruction) and produces less total mana. Yavimaya would turn Dark Depths, Karakas, and Wasteland into Forests, dramatically increasing green mana production. Boseiju's channel ability from hand could destroy the Chalice of the Void (set to 1) at instant speed whenever needed.

Cast Life from the Loam with zero land cards in the graveyard, returning nothing. While this does put Loam into the graveyard for future dredging, Malevolent Rumble was available at the same cost and would reveal top 4 cards (putting some into the graveyard to fuel future Loam dredges), find a permanent card, AND create an Eldrazi Spawn token.

Thespian's Stage was available and is the key combo piece with Dark Depths already on the battlefield. Copying Dark Depths with Thespian's Stage creates a copy with no ice counters, which immediately triggers the sacrifice to create Marit Lage (a 20/20 flying indestructible token). This is a well-known Legacy combo that wins the game quickly. Mox Diamond is a mana rock that requires discarding a land, which is far less impactful than assembling a combo kill. The player already has Life from the Loam in hand (and graveyard) to recur lands, and Thespian's Stage was the missing combo piece. With Stage + Dark Depths, the player could activate the combo as early as next turn with just 2 mana available.

Haiku Gramps had 2 mana available (Mox Diamond + Eldrazi Spawn token sacrifice) and could cast Life from the Loam to return Thespian's Stage, Yavimaya, and Wasteland from graveyard. Thespian's Stage + Dark Depths is the combo kill (20/20 Marit Lage). The player incorrectly assessed they had only 1 untapped mana source.

Life from the Loam would recover Thespian's Stage (plus Wasteland and Yavimaya) from the graveyard, enabling the Dark Depths + Thespian's Stage combo kill which is the deck's primary win condition. Dark Depths is already on the battlefield. Instead, a redundant Disruptor Flute was cast which provides marginal disruption when the opponent's Force of Will is already spent.

message: Select a Mox Opal to keep (Legendary Rule)?
annotation_description: When resolving the legendary rule for Mox Opal, Gem25F Libby kept the tapped copy and sacrificed the untapped one. This is backwards - keeping the untapped Mox Opal would preserve the ability to tap it for mana this turn (with Metalcraft active from Chalice of the Void, Seat of the Synod, and the kept Mox Opal). The reasoning given ('since one is already tapped, indicating its service, I shall preserve it') is completely inverted logic.
